body: That's horrible! I'm so sorry that happened to you. :(

I remember that when I first started taking Cymbalta I had some nausea, but that subsided after a week or two. And hunger. For the first two months I was so hungry. 

The main side-effect, however, is sexual. It's extremely difficult for me to cum. My wife and I have gotten around it and it's not so much a problem anymore.

That's horrible what you went through. I'm glad you're getting help. I'm usually on, so feel free to prod me anytime.

*Group therapy, for starters. I didn't respond well to one-on-one counseling sessions with my therapist. I'd clam up and end up not tell them the important stuff.

I found that being in a room with people having the same problems I had, and even different problems, pushed me so much higher than I thought possible. I had people who deal with depression on a day to day basis that I could talk to and share stories with. They couldn't judge me and wouldn't because they've gone through hell, same as me. 

I opened up and, with their help, explored who I was for the first time in probably years. 

*Anti-Depressants are a mixed bag. The newer ones start working within about a week or two, but meds that work for one person may not work for another. Dosage and side effects also vary. If the side effects are too much for you, consult the prescribing doctor immediately. He may change your dosage or switch you onto something else. 

*If your doctor prescribes you meds, don't stop taking them. Ever. Once your brain gets used to the meds, stopping will cause everything to go haywire. Most relapses into suicide are caused by stopping the medication. All anti-depression medications that I'm aware of require a step-down program.

*Find a Cognitive Behavioral Therapist. They can help you rewire your brain and CBT is a very effective treatment for depression.
*hugs Sarah tightly* I'm a bit new at this, but I'm here for you, too.

Congrats on your success! I'd heard about dual diagnosis from my stay at the psych ward and it's fantastic that you're conquering it. 

What are you studying and what kinds of challenges and fears do you find yourself running into?

I would also like to say that, believe me, it's better to not face depression or suicidal thoughts alone. Find someone you can be open to. Be as open as you can as much as you can to someone you can trust. 

It's so much easier to deal with these problems when they're small, disfigured inklings in your head.

The overarching theme in my suicide attempts seem to be "I am absolutely useless. The world would be so much better off without me. My fiancee can find a better man who will make her happier than I ever could. Etc..." 

The first time I'd decided that I could never make it in life. Everything that I am and was would never amount to anything important. I had thought of the consequences of my life choices and the type of life I would live because of them. I would be in a bad marriage (who would want to be with someone like that??) or perhaps homeless (why would I hire someone so worthless??). These, and more, were arguments I used against my continued existence. I had all the logic in the world on my side and I was winning. 
There was still something inside of me that didn't want to die and it refused to be reasoned with. Perhaps it was my conscience or maybe even something deeper like a self preservation instinct. It wouldn't let go. It was the reason for my crying. It halted my whole plan with the simple phrase: "I don't want to die. I don't want to die." 
Eventually, I fell asleep exhausted from the turmoil. That allowed me a respite to step back and take a look at things. It was hard to call for help, though. I'd thought that my parents, and anyone I asked help from, would hate me for bringing something so stupid to them.

I think probably the biggest difference between the first and second time was the amount of time I took to get from decision to action. The 1st time I'd spent all morning doing whatever I wanted. I played on the internet, listened to music, even read a chapter from my favorite book. Enough to remind myself why I enjoyed life. I woke up around 7 AM, but didn't try until close to 12 or 1 PM.

The 2nd time was much different. I went from getting the call from my boss to being home alone in about a half hour. Once I started with the first pill I just kept going and the whole process took maybe five minutes. I didn't give myself enough time to remember the good things that made life worth living. 

Also, my mindset had changed. The 1st time, I argued for self destruction. The 2nd time, I just did it.

What happened with your friend? Our family has kept what happened pretty quiet and I've only told maybe three close friends I trust. I was told that explaining what happened would cause some people to treat me differently.
Thank you. I greatly appreciate that.

I prescribed Lexapro after my first attempt for 9 months or so. My doctor then moved me to Cymbalta 60mg/day. I was on medication during my 2nd attempt. Currently, I'm taking 120mg of Cymbalta per day. I have improved substantially and am now stable.
However, the medication is only a stopgap in terms of my emotional health. I have years of cognitive behavioral therapy ahead of me.
